memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
"The LORD said to Moses and Aaron, 'These are the regulations for the Passover
meal: No foreigner may eat it. Any slave you have bought may eat it after you
have circumcised him, but a temporary resident or a hired worker may not eat
it.'" - Ex 12:43-45 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
At first glance this sounds exclusionary, so let us read it carefully.

The line is not drawn by race or nationality. It is drawn by covenant. A
foreigner who joined himself to Israel through circumcision, the sign of the
covenant, could eat. A bought slave could eat, once circumcised, which is a
remarkable statement of equality for the ancient world. But someone merely
passing through, with no covenant commitment, could not.

In other words, the meal belonged to those who belonged. It was not a matter of
where you were born but of whether you were in.

The New Testament keeps this principle for the Lord's Supper. Paul warns against
taking it carelessly and calls believers to examine themselves first (1 Cor
11:28). The table is for those who belong to Christ.

This is not about excluding people from God. Quite the opposite. The door to the
covenant was wide open to any foreigner willing to walk through it. What God
would not permit was the meal without the commitment, the symbol without the
substance.

He still cares more about our reality than our appearance.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Are you taking part in Christian things without having truly come to Christ?
2. How do you prepare your heart before the Lord's Supper?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Lord, I do not want the outward form without the inward reality. Search me and
make sure I truly belong to You. Amen.
